examples.ko: 심장이 쿵쾅 뛰어서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My heart was pounding so hard that I couldn't sleep.
The kids upstairs run around thumping every night.
My chest was thumping before the presentation.
Someone is banging loudly on the door outside.
I keep hearing banging noises from the construction site.
A heavy box fell with a loud bang.

explain: '쿵쿵'보다 더 요란하고 시끄럽게 부딪치거나 뛰는 소리에 써요. 층간소음 같은 소리에도 쓰고, 심장이 세게 뛰는 느낌에도 써요. 보통 '쿵쾅 뛰다', '쿵쾅 소리'처럼 뒤에 말이 이어져요.
explain_en: It is louder and noisier than '쿵쿵'. You can use it for thumping noises such as noise from the floor above, and also for a heart pounding hard. It is usually followed by another word, as in '쿵쾅 뛰다' or '쿵쾅 소리'.

examples.ko: 아이들이 밤늦게까지 쿵쾅대서 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: The kids keep thumping until late at night, so I can't sleep.
The neighbors keep banging around all day long.
Why are you stomping around like that?

examples.ko: 공사 때문에 아침부터 하루 종일 쿵쾅댔어요.
examples.en: The construction kept banging from morning all day long.

examples.ko: 그만 쿵쾅대고 조용히 좀 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please stop thumping around and be quiet.
I got nervous and my heart started pounding.

explain: '-대다'가 붙어서 크고 요란한 소리가 계속 반복된다는 느낌이 있어요. '쿵쾅거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요. 사람이 시끄럽게 걸을 때, 공사 소리, 심장 소리에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: The '-대다' ending gives the feeling that a loud noise keeps repeating. '쿵쾅거리다' means the same thing. You can use it for noisy walking, construction noise and a pounding heart.

examples.en: The person upstairs thumps around every night, and it's hard on me.
The little kid came down the stairs thumping.
My heart is thumping, so I can't fall asleep.
Please don't thump so loudly in the hallway.

examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 쿵쿵거리며 방을 나갔어요.
examples.en: He was angry and stomped out of the room.
I walked with heavy thuds, carrying a heavy load.

explain: 무겁고 둔한 소리가 계속 나는 것을 말해요. 발소리, 문 소리, 심장 뛰는 소리에 두루 써요. '쿵쿵대다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 화가 나서 일부러 발소리를 크게 내며 걸을 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes a heavy, dull sound that keeps repeating. It works for footsteps, doors and a heartbeat. It is nearly the same as '쿵쿵대다'. It is also common when someone walks off angrily, stamping loudly.

examples.ko: 며칠 잠을 못 자서 눈이 퀭해요.
examples.en: I haven't slept for days, so my eyes look sunken.
You've looked hollow-faced lately, so I was worried.
During exams, everyone's eyes look hollow.

examples.ko: 눈이 퀭한 친구를 보고 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I saw my friend with sunken eyes and bought him a meal.

examples.ko: 밤샘 근무 후에 거울을 보니 눈이 퀭했어요.
examples.en: After the all-night shift, my eyes looked sunken in the mirror.
After being sick for a long time, his cheeks became hollow.

explain: 주로 '눈이 퀭하다'처럼 피곤하거나 아파서 눈이 쑥 들어가고 기운이 없어 보일 때 써요. 볼이나 얼굴에도 쓸 수 있어요. 그냥 눈이 깊은 사람에게 쓰는 말이 아니라, 지치고 야윈 모습을 걱정하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '눈이 퀭하다' when someone's eyes look sunken and lifeless from tiredness or illness. You can also use it for cheeks or a face. It is not for people who simply have deep-set eyes; it carries a worried tone about someone looking worn out and thin.

examples.en: I comforted the family that was in deep sorrow.
My parents' kindness is truly immense.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 우리에게 크나큰 교훈이 됐어요.
examples.en: This incident became a great lesson for us.

examples.ko: 그분이 보여 준 크나큰 사랑을 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I can't forget the great love that person showed me.

examples.ko: 수상 소식은 우리 팀에게 크나큰 기쁨이에요.
examples.en: The news of the award is a huge joy for our team.
It was a huge mistake, but everyone forgave me.

explain: '아주 크다'를 강조하는 말인데, 보통 '크나큰 슬픔·기쁨·은혜·영향'처럼 감정이나 추상적인 것에 써요. 물건의 크기에는 잘 안 써요. 대화보다 글이나 연설, 감사 인사 같은 말투에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a stronger way of saying '크다' (big), usually in forms like '크나큰 슬픔/기쁨/은혜/영향' for feelings and abstract things. It is rarely used for the physical size of objects. It fits writing, speeches and thank-you messages better than casual talk.

examples.en: On holidays the whole family gathers at my eldest uncle's house.
I'm planning to visit my uncle's house this weekend.

examples.ko: 큰댁 사촌 형이 다음 달에 결혼한대요.
examples.en: I heard my cousin from my uncle's house is getting married next month.
My mother bought fruit to send to my uncle's house.
My uncle's house is in the countryside, so the yard is big.

examples.ko: 할아버지 제사 때문에 큰댁으로 가야 해요.
examples.en: I have to go to my uncle's house for my grandfather's memorial service.

explain: 아버지의 형, 곧 큰아버지의 집을 높여 부르는 말이에요. 말할 때는 '큰집'이라고도 해요. 아버지의 동생 집은 '작은집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the respectful word for the house of your father's older brother (큰아버지). People also say '큰집'. The house of your father's younger brother is '작은집'.

examples.en: I made up my mind and bought a new laptop.
Today I'll go all out and treat everyone.
I started this diet after a big decision, but it's hard.
I splurged and gave my parents some pocket money.

examples.ko: 이번 휴가에는 큰맘 먹고 해외여행을 가요.
examples.en: This vacation I'm taking the plunge and going abroad.

examples.ko: 큰맘을 먹지 않으면 운동을 시작하기 어려워요.
examples.en: Unless you really resolve to do it, it's hard to start exercising.

explain: 거의 '큰맘 먹고'의 꼴로 쓰여요. 평소에 망설이던 일을 큰 결심을 하고 할 때, 특히 돈을 쓸 때 많이 말해요. '큰마음'을 줄인 말이에요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 큰맘 먹고 비싼 식당에 갔어요.
phrases.en: Today I splurged and went to an expensive restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소에는 아끼거나 망설이던 일을 큰 결심을 하고 할 때 써요. 한턱내거나 비싼 물건을 살 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you make a big decision to do something you normally avoid or hold back on, such as treating people or buying something pricey.
phrases.en_equiv: to splurge; to take the plunge

explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '큰맘 먹고'. You use it when you finally decide to do something you normally hesitate over, especially when spending money. It is a short form of '큰마음'.

examples.ko: 그는 부동산 시장의 큰손으로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: He is known as a big player in the real estate market.

examples.ko: 해외 큰손들이 국내 주식을 사고 있어요.
examples.en: Big overseas investors are buying domestic stocks.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 큰손 손님이 오면 특별히 챙겨 줘요.
examples.en: This shop takes special care of big-spending customers.

examples.ko: 경매장에 큰손이 나타나서 가격이 확 올랐어요.
examples.en: A big buyer showed up at the auction and the price shot up.
Stock prices swing a lot depending on what the big players do.

examples.ko: 저는 큰손은 아니지만 매달 조금씩 투자해요.
examples.en: I'm not a big player, but I invest a little every month.

explain: 손이 큰 사람이 아니라, 증권·부동산·경매처럼 돈이 오가는 곳에서 큰돈을 움직이는 사람을 말해요. 반대로 적은 돈으로 투자하는 개인 투자자는 '개미'라고 해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 가게에서는 돈을 많이 쓰는 손님을 가리키기도 해요.
explain_en: It does not mean someone with large hands; it means a person who moves a lot of money in places like the stock market, real estate or auctions. Small individual investors are called '개미' (ants). It often appears in the news, and shops also use it for customers who spend a lot.

examples.en: If you underestimate your opponent, you'll pay dearly for it.

examples.ko: 준비도 안 하고 시험 보면 큰코다쳐요.
examples.en: If you take the exam without preparing, you'll get burned.
I took that person lightly and paid dearly for it.

examples.ko: 운전을 너무 자신하면 큰코다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you're overconfident about driving, you could end up in trouble.

examples.ko: 투자 공부 없이 뛰어들면 큰코다칠지도 몰라요.
examples.en: If you jump into investing without studying, you might get badly burned.
Be careful so you don't let your guard down and pay for it.

explain: 코를 다친다는 뜻이 아니라, 얕보거나 방심하다가 크게 실패하거나 손해를 본다는 뜻이에요. 주로 '그러다가 큰코다친다'처럼 경고나 충고로 말해요. '혼나다'는 야단을 맞는 것이고, '큰코다치다'는 자기 잘못된 판단 때문에 낭패를 보는 거예요.
explain_en: It does not mean hurting your nose; it means failing badly or suffering a loss because you underestimated something or let your guard down. It is mostly used as a warning, like '그러다가 큰코다친다'. '혼나다' means being scolded, while '큰코다치다' means getting into trouble because of your own poor judgment.

examples.en: My puppy goes around sniffing the floor.
My younger sibling has been sniffing for a while to figure out the smell.
The cat sniffed the unfamiliar bag for a long time.
My nose is stuffed, so I keep sniffling.
Stop sniffing around and come eat.
The police dog sniffed the bag and then stopped.

explain: 코로 냄새를 맡으려고 숨을 짧게 자꾸 들이쉬는 소리나 모습이에요. 강아지나 고양이에게 많이 쓰고, 코가 막혔을 때도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 조금 우스꽝스럽거나 장난스러운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes taking short, repeated sniffs through the nose to smell something, or the sound of that. It is often used for dogs and cats, and also for a stuffy nose. Used for a person, it sounds a little comical or playful.

examples.en: My friends were giggling behind me, and it bothered me.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 자꾸 키득대면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't keep snickering during class.
My younger sibling is giggling while reading a comic book.
What's so funny that you're giggling?
The kids were secretly snickering and got caught by the teacher.
On my way home from work I giggled to myself looking at my phone.

explain: '깔깔'은 크게 소리 내어 웃는 것이고, '키득대다'는 소리를 죽이고 짧게 끊어서 웃는 거예요. '킬킬대다'는 놀리듯 더 짓궂고, '키득거리다'는 같은 말이에요. 수업 중에 뒤에서 몰래 웃는 장면에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '깔깔' is loud, open laughter, while '키득대다' is short, muffled laughter. '킬킬대다' is more mischievous and teasing, and '키득거리다' means the same as this word. It fits scenes like secretly laughing in the back of a class.

examples.ko: 친구가 농담을 하자 다 같이 킬킬거렸어요.
examples.en: When my friend told a joke, we all snickered together.
The kids in the back row snicker all through class.
I'm snickering to myself while watching a cartoon.
What's making you snicker like that?
The mischievous kids looked at each other and snickered.
When someone fell, the kids looked on snickering.

explain: '키득거리다'와 비슷하지만 좀 더 짓궂고 장난스럽게, 놀리듯이 웃는 느낌이 있어요. 남의 실수나 우스운 장면을 보고 웃을 때 잘 어울려요. 윗사람 앞에서 이렇게 웃으면 예의 없어 보일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '키득거리다' but has a more mischievous, teasing feel. It suits laughing at someone's mistake or a funny scene. Laughing this way in front of a superior can look rude.

examples.ko: 타교 학생도 이 도서관을 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Students from other schools can also use this library.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 타교와 축구 시합을 해요.
examples.en: Next week we have a soccer match against another school.
A teacher from another school came to give a special lecture.

examples.ko: 타교 수업을 들으려면 학점 교환을 신청해야 해요.
examples.en: To take classes at another school, you have to apply for a credit exchange.

examples.ko: 저는 타교 친구들과 같이 동아리를 해요.
examples.en: I do a club activity together with friends from other schools.
I came from another school, so this school feels unfamiliar.

explain: 자기 학교가 아닌 다른 학교를 말해요. 공지나 규정, 글에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '다른 학교'라고 해요. 반대로 우리 학교는 '본교'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a school other than your own. It appears mainly in notices, rules and writing, while in speech people say '다른 학교'. Your own school is '본교'.

examples.ko: 가뭄에 밭의 잎이 누렇게 타들어 가요.
examples.en: In the drought, the leaves in the field are withering and turning yellow.

examples.ko: 심지가 천천히 타들어 가는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the wick slowly burning down.
The edge of the paper touched the fire and charred.

examples.ko: 가뭄이 길어지자 논바닥이 갈라지고 벼가 타들었어요.
examples.en: As the drought dragged on, the rice paddies cracked and the rice plants withered.

examples.ko: 햇볕이 너무 강해서 화단의 풀이 다 타들었어요.
examples.en: The sun was so strong that the grass in the flower bed all dried up.
The tip that touched the flame was charred black.

explain: '타다'와 달리 불이 끝에서부터 서서히 안쪽으로 먹어 들어가는 모습, 또는 가뭄과 햇볕에 식물이 말라 죽어 가는 모습을 말해요. 보통 '타들어 가다' 형태로 써요. 마음이 몹시 불안하고 답답할 때 '속이 타들어 가다'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 합격 발표를 기다리는 동안 속이 타들어 갔어요.
phrases.en: I was on pins and needles while waiting for the results to be announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정과 초조함 때문에 마음이 몹시 애가 탈 때 써요. 실제로 몸이 타는 게 아니라 마음 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when worry and impatience make you extremely anxious. It describes your state of mind, not anything physically burning.
phrases.en_equiv: to be on pins and needles; to be eaten up with worry

explain_en: Unlike plain '타다' (to burn), it describes fire creeping inward from the edge, or plants drying up and dying in drought and strong sun. It is usually used as '타들어 가다'. It is also used figuratively, as in '속이 타들어 가다', when you feel very anxious.

examples.en: My grandmother is unwinding a skein of yarn.
I bought two skeins of yarn at the market.

examples.ko: 고운 명주실 한 타래가 선물로 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A skein of fine silk thread came in as a gift.
The cat got tangled in the skein of yarn and is whining.

examples.ko: 소면 한 타래면 두 사람이 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: One bundle of thin noodles is enough for two people.

examples.ko: 이 엉킨 타래부터 천천히 풀어 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll slowly untangle this tangled skein first.

explain: 실이나 국수 같은 긴 것을 사려서 한 뭉치로 묶은 것을 말해요. '털실 두 타래'처럼 세는 단위로도 써요. 보통 '실타래'로 많이 말하는데, 실타래가 엉키다처럼 일이 복잡하게 꼬였다는 비유에도 써요.
explain_en: It is a coil of long things like thread or noodles gathered into one bundle. It is also used as a counting unit, as in '털실 두 타래'. It is often said as '실타래', which is also used figuratively when a matter gets tangled up.

examples.en: Fortunately it's not serious, just a bruise.
I fell on the stairs and bruised my knee.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 타박상에는 냉찜질이 좋다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said a cold compress is good for bruises.
I collided while playing soccer and got a bruise on my thigh.
Because of the contusion, I got a big bruise.

examples.ko: 가벼운 타박상이라 며칠 쉬면 나을 거래요.
examples.en: They say it's a mild bruise, so it'll heal after a few days' rest.

explain: 부딪히거나 맞아서 피부는 찢어지지 않았지만 속에 멍이 들고 붓는 상처를 말해요. 긁히거나 쓸린 상처는 '찰과상'이라고 해요. 병원이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '멍들었다'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is an injury from a hit or collision where the skin is not broken but the tissue beneath is bruised and swollen. A scrape on the surface is called '찰과상'. It is the word used at hospitals and in the news, while in daily talk people may just say '멍들었다'.

examples.en: The child trudged away with a tired face.

examples.ko: 비 오는 길을 타박타박 걸어서 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: I trudged home along the rainy road.

examples.ko: 할머니가 지팡이를 짚고 타박타박 시장에 가세요.
examples.en: Grandmother leans on her cane and walks slowly to the market.

examples.ko: 먼 길을 타박타박 걷다 보니 해가 졌어요.
examples.en: As I trudged along the long road, the sun went down.
After work I plodded home with my tired body.
The sound of plodding footsteps gradually came closer.

explain: 힘없이 느리게 걷는 모습이나 그 발소리를 나타내요. 보통 '타박타박 걷다', '타박타박 걸어가다'처럼 써요. '터벅터벅'도 비슷하게 지친 걸음에 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes walking slowly and wearily, or the sound of such footsteps. It is usually used as '타박타박 걷다' or '타박타박 걸어가다'. '터벅터벅' is a similar word for tired walking.

examples.en: Don't be so hard on someone just because they made a mistake.
Mom scolded my younger sibling for coming home late.
There was a customer who complained that the food was salty.

examples.ko: 남의 잘못을 자꾸 타박하면 사이가 나빠져요.
examples.en: If you keep criticizing others' faults, your relationship will get worse.

examples.ko: 친구의 부족한 점을 타박하지 않고 도와줬어요.
examples.en: I helped my friend without criticizing his shortcomings.
She said she was upset because her mother-in-law criticized her cooking.

explain: 잘못이나 부족한 점, 불만을 말로 나무라거나 흠잡을 때 써요. '야단치다'가 크게 혼내는 느낌이라면, '타박하다'는 핀잔주고 투덜대는 느낌이에요. '음식 타박', '타박을 주다/듣다'처럼도 써요. '타박상'과 소리가 같지만 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used when you criticize or find fault with someone's mistakes, shortcomings or something you dislike. While '야단치다' feels like a big scolding, '타박하다' feels like nagging and grumbling. It also appears in phrases like '음식 타박' and '타박을 주다/듣다'. It sounds like '타박상', but they are different words.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 너무 타산적이라 친해지기 어려워요.
examples.en: That person is too calculating, so it's hard to get close to him.
Calculating relationships don't last long.
If you make friends with calculation, you end up lonely.
I'm worried that I might be too calculating.

examples.ko: 결혼을 너무 타산적으로 생각하는 건 아닌가요?
examples.en: Aren't you thinking about marriage in too calculating a way?
He has a calculating personality that only cares about profit.

explain: 자기에게 이익이 되는지 손해가 되는지부터 따지는 태도를 말하고, 좋은 뜻은 아니에요. 실제로는 '타산적이다', '타산적인 사람', '타산적으로'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '계산적이다', '따지다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes an attitude of first weighing whether something benefits or costs you, and it is not a compliment. In practice it appears as '타산적이다', '타산적인 사람' or '타산적으로'. In everyday talk people also say '계산적이다' or '따지다'.

examples.en: If you work out of sheer habit, your mistakes increase.

examples.ko: 오랜 타성에서 벗어나려고 새로운 방법을 시도했어요.
examples.en: I tried a new method to break free from my old rut.
Because of force of habit, I repeat the same mistake.
As my time at the company gets longer, I fall into a rut.
I changed jobs because I wanted to break out of my rut.
There's no fun in work you do just out of habit.

explain: 오래 해 와서 굳어져, 생각 없이 그냥 하게 되는 습관을 말해요. 대부분 나쁜 뜻이에요. 좋든 나쁘든 몸에 밴 '습관'과 달리, 변화 없이 매너리즘에 빠진 느낌이에요. '타성에 젖다', '타성에서 벗어나다' 같은 말과 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It means a habit that has set in over a long time and makes you act without thinking, and it is almost always negative. Unlike '습관', which can be good or bad, it carries a feeling of being stuck in a rut. It often appears in phrases such as '타성에 젖다' and '타성에서 벗어나다'.
